summary: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on the lossless MXFP4-CSF checkpoint decodes 3-4% faster, as fast as the uncompressed checkpoint: compact W4A8 kernels read the compressed expert scales inline
compatibility: No user action required. B12X_W4A8_CSF_INLINE=0 at weight preparation restores the per-call scale expansion; B12X_W4A8_CSF_INLINE_MAX_TOKENS (default 1536) sets the largest planned call that reads inline scales.
details: Compact W4A8 MoE kernels (intermediate size 64 mod 128: micro FC1/FC2 and split M16 FC1/FC2) stage 96-byte compressed scale tiles and rebuild each thread's E8M0 scale words in registers, so calls planned for up to 1536 tokens run no routed-expert scale expansion. Larger, compute-bound calls expand every expert's scales once from the same storage and run the native kernels. Outputs are bit-identical.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP4 with DSpark on four RTX PRO 6000 Max-Q, lossless CSF checkpoint, against the per-call expansion: decode C8 816 vs 787, C16 1,108 vs 1,069, C32 1,645 vs 1,581 tok/s (the uncompressed checkpoint: 807, 1,105, 1,612); 8K/32K prefill unchanged. KV cache 12.79M tokens vs 13.11M (inline storage 0.33 GiB per GPU) and 9.73M uncompressed.
The inline storage is built outside the caller's allocator pool: built inside it under vLLM's load-time allocator settings, it kept about 1 GiB per GPU of freed pages mapped.
